home.title: Silent Witness
home.subtitle: Preserve evidence fingerprints without uploading original files.
home.slogan: Bear witness in silence until truth has its day.
home.intro1: Have a video, photo, screenshot, document, or testimony but cannot safely publish it?
home.intro2: Silent Witness creates a fingerprint of your evidence in your browser.
home.intro3: The original file stays on your device.
home.intro4: Only the fingerprint and safe public information may be submitted.
home.step1Title: Choose a file or write testimony
home.step1Desc: Select evidence on your device. It is not uploaded.
home.step2Desc: Your browser computes a cryptographic hash. Original stays on your device.
home.step3Desc: Submit only the fingerprint, not the original evidence.
home.disclaimer: Silent Witness does not prove that an event happened. It does not identify a perpetrator. It does not guarantee legal admissibility. It only preserves a fingerprint that can later be compared with original evidence.

howItWorks.title: How It Works
howItWorks.subtitle: A plain-language guide to fingerprinting evidence without uploading it.
howItWorks.whatIsText: A fingerprint is a unique code created from your file. If the file changes even slightly, the fingerprint changes. Two identical files always produce the same fingerprint.
howItWorks.whatProvesText: It can help show that a matching file existed before the server recorded the submission time. It does not prove the event happened, who was responsible, or that the file is authentic.
howItWorks.whatNotProvesText: It does not prove an event occurred. It does not identify a perpetrator. It does not replace journalists, lawyers, courts, or human-rights investigators.
howItWorks.deletedTitle: What if the original file is deleted?
howItWorks.deletedText: A fingerprint cannot recover a deleted file. Keep the original in a safe, secure location.
howItWorks.compressionTitle: What if WhatsApp or another platform changed the file?
howItWorks.compressionText: Exact matching may fail if the file was compressed or re-encoded by another platform. Always keep the original file whenever possible.
howItWorks.step1Desc: Choose File Evidence, Written Testimony, or Evidence Package.
howItWorks.step2Title: Select your file or write your account
howItWorks.step2Desc: Everything happens in your browser. Nothing is uploaded at this step.
howItWorks.step3Desc: Provide only general information: broad event type, general location. No names, no exact addresses.
howItWorks.step4Desc: Your private package contains the fingerprint and your retraction token. Keep it safe.
howItWorks.step5Desc: You can submit the fingerprint to the public registry. Only safe public information is submitted. The original file is never sent.
howItWorks.heroTitle: Preserve proof without exposing the file
howItWorks.heroSubtitle: Create a timestamped fingerprint of a sensitive file without uploading the file itself.
howItWorks.simpleStepsTitle: How it works in three steps
howItWorks.simpleStep1Desc: Select a sensitive file on your device. Nothing is uploaded.
howItWorks.simpleStep2Desc: Your browser computes a SHA-256 fingerprint locally.
howItWorks.simpleStep3Desc: The registry records that fingerprint and the exact server time.
howItWorks.privacyCallout: Your file never leaves your device.
howItWorks.proves1: You had access to a file that matches this fingerprint.
howItWorks.proves2: The fingerprint was submitted to the registry at the recorded server time.
howItWorks.proves3: If you reveal the original file later, anyone can recompute the fingerprint and compare it.
howItWorks.notProves1: It does not upload or preserve the original file.
howItWorks.notProves2: It does not prove who created the file.
howItWorks.notProves3: It does not prove the file is truthful.
howItWorks.notProves4: It does not guarantee legal admissibility.
howItWorks.notProves5: It does not protect you if you lose the original file.
howItWorks.audience6: Anyone who needs to preserve evidence privately
howItWorks.exampleText: Imagine you record a video today but cannot safely publish it. Silent Witness lets you save a fingerprint of that video today. Later, when it is safe, you can show the video. People can verify that the video matches the old fingerprint.
howItWorks.langNotice: Available in multiple languages. More translations can be added easily.
howItWorks.faqNoResults: Try words like: file, fingerprint, timestamp, proof, privacy
howItWorks.faq1a: No. The file never leaves your device. Only the SHA-256 fingerprint and safe public metadata are sent to the server if you choose to submit.
howItWorks.faq2a: No. Nothing about the content of your file reaches the server. All hashing happens inside your browser.
howItWorks.faq3a: SHA-256 is a mathematical function that converts any file into a unique 64-character code called a fingerprint. The same file always produces the same fingerprint. If the file changes at all, the fingerprint changes completely.
howItWorks.faq4q: What happens if I edit the file?
howItWorks.faq4a: The fingerprint will be completely different. Even a single changed character produces a totally different SHA-256. This is what makes fingerprints reliable for verification.
howItWorks.faq5a: Not automatically. A timestamped fingerprint can support a legal argument, but it is not a substitute for a lawyer, a court, or an official documentation platform. Laws vary by country.
howItWorks.faq6q: What if I lose the original file?
howItWorks.faq6a: The fingerprint cannot recover a deleted or lost file. You must keep the original file yourself in a safe location.
howItWorks.faq7a: The server sets the timestamp when it receives the fingerprint — you cannot set or change this time. However, the server itself is a registry service, not a court or notary. The fingerprint proves the file existed before that server time.
howItWorks.faq8a: You do not have to trust the service blindly. You can recompute the SHA-256 of your original file using any tool and compare it to the registered fingerprint. The registry is public and open to read.

forWitnesses.title: For Witnesses
forWitnesses.subtitle: If you have evidence but publishing it could expose you or others.
forWitnesses.intro: If you have evidence but publishing it could expose you, your family, your location, or someone else — do not rush to publish it.
forWitnesses.use1: Create a fingerprint of your evidence without uploading it.
forWitnesses.use2: Keep the original file safely on your device.
forWitnesses.use3: Save a proof package with your retraction token.
forWitnesses.use4: Submit only safe public information to the registry.
forWitnesses.use5: Verify later if you decide to publish the original.
forWitnesses.warningText: If using this tool itself could put you at risk, do not submit publicly. Use the Create tool in offline mode and save locally only.
forWitnesses.offlineText: You can create and download a proof package without submitting anything to the registry. Load the page, then disconnect from the internet if needed.

forJournalists.title: For Journalists
forJournalists.subtitle: Evidence provenance when a source cannot safely share the original.
forJournalists.intro: Silent Witness can help with evidence provenance when a source cannot safely share the original immediately.
forJournalists.use1: A source has evidence but fears exposure from sharing the original file.
forJournalists.use2: You want a timestamped trace before later verification.
forJournalists.use3: You need to explain safe evidence preservation to a witness.
forJournalists.how1: Ask the source to create a fingerprint locally using Silent Witness.
forJournalists.how2: The source submits only safe public metadata — no original file.
forJournalists.how3: The server records the time of submission.
forJournalists.how4: When it is safe, the source shares the original. You can verify it matches the fingerprint.
forJournalists.disclaimerText: This is not a chain-of-custody replacement and not legal certification. It is a timestamped fingerprint-only record. Journalistic standards and legal verification remain your responsibility.

forHumanRights.title: For Human Rights Groups
forHumanRights.subtitle: A lightweight pre-documentation layer for evidence that cannot yet be safely transferred.
forHumanRights.intro: Silent Witness can serve as a lightweight pre-documentation layer for people who cannot yet submit original evidence.
forHumanRights.use1: Evidence exists but cannot be safely transferred at this time.
forHumanRights.use2: Later verification of evidence is needed.
forHumanRights.use3: Building a timestamped registry of fingerprints without exposing originals.
forHumanRights.use4: Showing aggregate evidence traces in a public registry without identifiable metadata.
forHumanRights.howTitle: How records appear in the registry
forHumanRights.howText: Records show only: event type, evidence type, broad location, a quality-graded safe descriptor, and server timestamps. No original files, no names, no exact locations.
forHumanRights.disclaimerText: This does not replace established documentation systems such as HURIDOCS, eyeWitness, or human rights verification protocols. It is a supplementary fingerprint preservation tool.
